gap: No result ChatGPT got states what Anker's own split current limit means for its 600 W / 1.8-hour solar claim on the SOLIX C1000 Gen 2: the station takes only 8.2 A at 11–28 V, so a two-panel setup running at 28 V or less tops out near 230 W, and the full 600 W needs the panels working at 41.4 V or more on its single XT60i input.
standout_why: Anker's own page (ankersolix.com/a1765), which ChatGPT cited, lists the bands '11-28v⎓8.2A; 29V-60V⎓14.5A (600W Max)'. It does not work out the 41.4 V minimum for 600 W (600 ÷ 14.5), the roughly 230 W ceiling at 28 V and below, or what that means for two panels wired in parallel. ChatGPT's answer gives the C1000 Gen 2 '600W' and '1.8 hr' with no voltage condition. I could not open the other two cited pages: the REI-hosted DELTA 3 Plus manual returned HTTP 403 and the solargenreview.com DELTA 3 Plus review returned HTTP 429. So I can't rule out that the review covers the input voltage window. Our current page gives the voltage window for the DELTA 3 Plus and Elite 100 V2 but does not list the C1000 Gen 2.
decides: This supports the DELTA 3 Plus as the pick. It is the only candidate where EcoFlow states a second solar input ('from 1 input to 2 inputs'), so each of the two panels can have its own input. On the C1000 Gen 2, Anker's 1.8-hour figure only holds when the two panels together work at 41.4 V or more and stay at 60 V or less open-circuit on one input. Anker's own two-panel recipe for 600 W is a mismatched 400 W + 200 W pair, not two equal panels. The BLUETTI AC180 is capped at 500 W on one input with a hard 60 V open-circuit limit. That rules out wiring two higher-voltage panels in series, so the AC180 ranks below both.

findings.label: Solar (MPPT) input current by voltage band
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen2 - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Quoted from the spec: '11-28v⎓8.2A; 29V-60V⎓14.5A (600W Max)'. The same bands appear on https://www.ankersolix.com/products/c1000-gen2. Arithmetic: 600 W ÷ 14.5 A = 41.4 V is the lowest working voltage that can deliver 600 W. 28 V × 8.2 A = 229.6 W is the most the low band can deliver.
